evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-20"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-20". The same request with a different title returned 201 with dueDate "2026-12-01". A POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/1 {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. PATCH /todos/1 {"dueDate":"2026-10-19"} returned 200 with the new date. PATCH /todos/4 set the date to 2026-10-01 (200), then null again (200).
evidence.AC3: These all returned HTTP 400 with the error 'dueDate must be a real date in YYYY-MM-DD format or null': POST with dueDate 2026-02-30, POST with 21.10.2026, POST with 2026-10-21T10:00:00Z, and PATCH with 2026-13-01.
evidence.AC4: Today in UTC is 2026-10-21. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the todo due 2026-10-19. A todo due today, a todo due 2026-12-01, a todo with no due date, and a done todo with a due date of 2026-01-01 were all excluded. The done todo showed overdue:false.
evidence.AC5: The page at / showed a <time> element with the due date for each todo that has one: 2026-10-19, 2026-10-21, 2026-12-01 and 2026-01-01. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot only the 'past' todo (due 2026-10-19) carried the text '· überfällig'. The todos due today, in the future, without a date, and done with a past date had no such marker.
evidence.AC7: The page had a button labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it set it to pressed and cut the list to the single overdue todo, 'past'.
